Latin word

internōscō

internōscō, internōscere, internōvī, internōtum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; the second thing with ā/ab + ablative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

tell apart, tell (one) from (another)

In this lexicon

  • distinguish

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.18 (by chapter): māter geminōs internōscit (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Men. prol. 20 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • sēcernī blandus amīcus ā vērō et internōscī potest

    a flatterer can be told apart from a true friend and distinguished from himCic. Amic. 25 (by chapter; Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for distinguish

  • fētūs suōs nōn distinguunt ferae et sē in alimentum pariter omnium sternunt

    wild animals make no difference between their young, and lie down to feed them all alikeSen. Ep. 66.26

    In the entry for distinguish

  • nōtum ignōtumque quantum ad jūs hospitis nēmō discernit

    as far as a guest’s rights go, nobody makes a difference between a friend and a strangerTac. Germ. 21.3
